text:
Say it, say it again, and repeat once more

that you love me, though that repeated word,

on your lips, recalls the cuckoo's song.

And do not forget that fresh spring never


came to mountain or plain, to valley or woods,

in its whole greenness, without the cuckoo's voice.

It greets me in the shadows, my beloved, uncertain,

that voice of a spirit, and in my anguished doubt,


I cry: "Say again that you love me!" Who

fears an excess of stars, though they fill the heavens,

or an excess of flowers girdling the whole year?


Say that you love me, say that you love me: renew

the silver ringing; but think, my beloved,

of loving me also with the soul, in silence.

translation.title: Say It, Say It Again
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated request for spoken love while preserving the final turn toward silent soul-love.
